name: bluewater-18-who-gets-the-job
lines: One homeowner. One leaking kitchen. Five contractors who all want the job.
Only one of them will get it. And it's not the one you think.
This is, Who Gets The Job.
Tonight's homeowner has a faucet that drips, a cabinet that's swelling, and exactly one evening to pick somebody.
Let's meet our contestants. They're all made up. You've hired every one of them.
Contestant one. The Ghost. Great reviews. Has not answered a phone since the Olympics.
Contestant two. The Bargain. Whatever the other guy said, he'll do it for less. He hasn't asked what the job is.
Contestant three. The Professor. Thirty years of experience, and he will tell you about all thirty.
Contestant four. The Logo. No face. No photos. Just a clip art wrench, and a dream.
And contestant five. Rita. Six years in business. Kind of nervous. Brought a pen.
Round one. First impressions.
Our homeowner searches on her phone. She gives each of them four seconds. That's generous.
The Ghost. Lovely photos. From twenty eighteen. Is that even his van anymore?
The Logo. It's a wrench. She squints. Still a wrench.
The Professor's profile has eleven paragraphs. She scrolls. It keeps going.
Rita. A photo of Rita, next to a sink, giving a thumbs up. It's a little awkward. It's also a human being.
The Logo has been eliminated. Nobody hires a wrench.
Round two. The phone call.
She calls all four. One at a time.
The Ghost. It rings. And rings. Then a voicemail greeting, from a man who sounds surprised he owns a phone.
The Bargain picks up on the first ring. How much is the other guy charging? She hasn't said hello yet.
The Professor answers, and explains the history of compression fittings. She puts him on speaker, and makes dinner.
Rita picks up. Hi, this is Rita. What's going on with your kitchen?
A question. About her kitchen. The homeowner has to sit down.
The Ghost has been eliminated. He does not know. He will never know.
Round three. The quote. Three contestants remain.
The Bargain goes first. He texts one number. No words. Just a number, and a thumbs up.
It's the lowest. The crowd goes wild. He's winning. This might be over.
The Professor sends a nine page document. Page four has a diagram. Nobody knows what it's a diagram of.
And Rita sends one page. What's included. When she can start. What happens if it leaks again.
The homeowner reads it twice. Then she reads it to her husband.
The Professor has been eliminated. His document will be studied by scholars.
The final two.
The Bargain. And Rita. And he is cheaper. By a lot.
Our homeowner picks up her phone. Her thumb is over his name.
She has one last question. She texts them both. Does your price include fixing the cabinet?
Rita answers in six minutes. Yes. It's on the quote. Line three.
The Bargain answers the next day. Cabinet is extra. So is the faucet. So is showing up.
And just like that, the cheapest price in the room became the most expensive.
Rita gets the job.
So what just happened?
She didn't pick the best plumber. She has no idea who the best plumber is. Nobody does.
She picked the one who was easiest to hire.
Four rounds. Four tiny things.
A real face in the photo.
A human on the phone, who asked about her kitchen.
A quote she could read to her husband.
And an answer in six minutes, not a day.
None of those cost money. All of them beat a lower price.
Now, the honest part. Sometimes the cheap guy wins anyway. Some customers only see the number.
And no checklist can promise you the job.
But most people aren't hiring the best. They're hiring the one who made it easy.
Three weeks later. The faucet doesn't drip.
Our homeowner leaves a review. Five stars. She showed up. She texted back. Hire Rita.
The Ghost reads it on his phone. He has two hundred and six unread messages.
That's our show. Be a Rita.
If you want your business to be the easy one to hire, that's what we do. Bluewater Co dot C A.
